title: Malleable sequence-length consolidator: pad-shedding with kernel-affinity scheduling
creator: Elena Martinez
description: Problem: Significant token-cost waste from padding across mixed-length requests. Current bucketers reduce padding but are static w.r.t kernel performance characteristics and prefill vs decode scheduling. This ticket implements a "malleable sequence-length consolidator" that combines runtime kernel-affinity signals with a pad-shedding strategy to reshape micro-batches at prefill time and opportunistically during decode.
goals: Reduce mean tokens/payload padding by >= 20% on mixed-length workloads
Maintain p50 latency within existing SLOs and keep p99 tail impact <= +5ms where possible
Add kernel-affinity heuristics so scheduler prefers groupings that map to fast kernels for common seqlen ranges
Expose telemetry for bucket composition, pad-shed bytes, and kernel selection decisions
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Introduce a lightweight runtime estimator that tracks observed kernel latency per (model, seqlen-bin, hardware affinity). 2) When forming micro-batches, prefer merging short sequences into a malleable slot that can be prefinned to the KV cache with compacted prefixes (pad-shedding). 3) For decode-heavy requests, allow elastic re-bucketing mid-decode if decode queue latency indicates idle kernels that can accept coalesced requests. 4) Apply a conservative fallback policy: if kernel-affinity heuristic uncertainty > threshold, revert to existing stable bucketer.
tradeoffs: Aggressive pad-shedding reduces token cost but can add CPU overhead for compaction and extra copy operations — may increase p99 under high contention. Kernel-affinity biases improve throughput for common paths but risk starving rare-seqlen kernels. We mitigate with runtime confidence scoring and a decay window for affinity counters.
implementation_plan: Telemetry: augment existing bucketer metrics with per-bin kernel latency histograms
Estimator: implement lightweight online latency estimator scoped to model+bin+backend
Scheduler: extend packer to produce malleable slots with compacted prefix objects and pad-shedding markers
Prefill: add path to prefill using compacted KV entries where compatible
Decode: prototype mid-decode re-bucketing logic guarded by safety checks
E2E: perf harness runs for three production traffic traces and compare tokens-per-request and latency distributions
Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback on quality/latency regressions
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark A (mixed chat workload) shows >=20% reduction in padded tokens per request and >=15% reduction in token cost on average
End-to-end p50 latency change <= +1ms; p99 change <= +5ms across benchmarks
No increase in model output divergence above noise baseline (quality checks pass for provided eval prompts)
Telemetry surfaces kernel-affinity confidence and pad-shed ratios per minute
PRs merged and feature flag behind runtime-config with immediate rollback capability
risks: Extra memory churn from prefix compaction objects; complex interactions with KV cache eviction semantics; need to validate correctness across quantized kernels. Potentially masks root-cause capacity imbalances if used as a permanent patch without addressing upstream scheduling bottlenecks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for estimator and packer; synthetic microbench for seqlen mixes (short/medium/long); canary on non-critical model fleet for 72h; compare p99 traces and kernel selection logs. Add chaos test that simulates kernel slowdowns to ensure fallbacks work.
